newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns on foreign borrowing guarantees.
newsitem.headline: China warns on foreign borrowing guarantees.

text.p: China warned state companies and government departments on Tuesday that they should not provide guarantees on foreign borrowings unless they were specifically given permission by the State Council (cabinet).
The warning, a repetition of existing regulations, was issued after the People's Bank of China, or central bank, had discovered serious violations of the rules, the official Xinhua news agency said.
It gave no specific examples of any recent financial guarantees to foreign entities but it stated that any guarantees found to be in violation of the regulations would be declared invalid.
Management of the Chinese entity involved could be penalised under foreign exchange regulations and in severe cases, punishment might be applied under criminal law, the agency said.
China has been trying to control the loss of state assets.
In the past it had set regulations specifying which government agencies were eligible to borrow or guarantee loans from abroad in a bid to return control to the central government over foreign debt.

Local governments and government corporations have at times raised funds from abroad without permission of the central government, occasionally failing to make repayment. Central government officials fear this will hurt China's credit record.
